subject: Hosted API latency SLO proposal — tiered snapshotting & measurement approach
messages:
From: Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — measurement window concern

Hi Soojin / team,

Thanks again for walking us through the hosted API options yesterday. Before we move to contract language, we need one more clarification on how you measure p50 / p95. Our primary concern: short, sharp bursts (e.g., short-lived traffic spikes during product launches or marketing events) can push p95 above our target for a handful of hours even though the experience is fine for most users.

Two asks from Brightline:
- Can Redwood propose an alternative measurement method that reduces sensitivity to isolated minute-level spikes but still captures sustained tail latency?
- What proofpoints (canary results / historical evidence) can you provide to show the alternative won't mask real regressions?

We'd prefer something that keeps the contract simple (p50/p95 targets) but avoids triggering credits for transient load events. Happy to hop on a short call next week.

Thanks,
Ava Morales
Head of Platform — Brightline

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Brightline Ops <ops@brightline.ai>, Ava Morales <ava.morales@brightline.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — measurement window concern

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear ask. We hear you. Below is a concrete proposal that keeps contract language to a simple p50 / p95 commitment but changes the measurement approach to reduce noisy triggers from short spikes.

Summary (high level):
- Contract: p50 and p95 targets unchanged (explicit ms targets in SLA).
- Measurement model: tiered snapshotting with guarded tail truncation (keeps sensitivity to sustained degradation, reduces credits from transient micro-spikes).

Proposal details:
1) Tiered snapshotting
   - We compute 1-minute latency samples across all requests as usual.
   - For p50: report the median of the full-day 1-minute samples (unchanged).
   - For p95: compute rolling 5-minute snapshots every 15 minutes (i.e., 00:00-00:05, 00:15-00:20, ...), take the 95th percentile within each snapshot, then aggregate those snapshot p95s over the billing window and report the 95th percentile of the snapshot-level p95s.
   - Rationale: a single 1-minute spike will only affect at most one snapshot and is unlikely to move the snapshot-level p95 distribution unless spikes are sustained across multiple snapshots.

2) Guarded tail truncation (operational carveout)
   - We apply an exponential-decay weighting to snapshot p95s from the last 24 hours to reduce the impact of an isolated, brief tail event when it is not indicative of continued degradation.
   - We exclude scheduled maintenance windows (customers and Redwood agree on maintenance calendar) and cloud provider outage events validated by a cross-check with provider status pages.

3) Evidence & canary plan
   - Pilot: 30-day pilot using Brightline's production traffic in our hosted environment with both the standard rolling-sample p95 and the tiered-snapshot p95 computed in parallel.
   - We will share a daily CSV with snapshot p95s and raw request-level latency for the period (sanitized).
   - Pass criteria: the tiered approach must not hide regressions identified by our eval prompts/tracebacks and must reduce false-positive credit triggers vs the baseline by > 60% on historical launch events (we'll run a retrospective backtest during onboarding).

4) Operational fallbacks and credits
   - If tiered snapshotting is adopted and we later discover it masked a real regression, we will revert to the baseline measurement for the affected billing window and apply the agreed credit policy.

Next steps:
- I attached a short write-up (slo_proposal_v2.pdf) that diagrams the snapshots and weighting math.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute call on Wed 12/3 to walk the pilot timeline and acceptance criteria?

Thanks — happy to refine the math if your ops folks want different snapshot cadence.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — measurement window concern

Ava / team — quick technical note from infra side on feasibility and instrumentation:

- The serving runtime already emits 1-minute latency histograms per model shard. Implementing the 5-minute snapshot aggregation + snapshot-level p95 is a straightforward additional aggregation job; we can run it alongside the existing aggregator without impacting production serving.
- For the pilot we will provide: (a) raw 1-minute histograms, (b) computed snapshot p95s, (c) the snapshot-level p95 time-series (CSV). I've attached a sample export (latency_evidence.csv) from a comparable customer pilot last quarter so you can see the format.
- Operational checks: we will add a simple provider-status cross-check that tags snapshots overlapping a provider incident; those tagged snapshots will be excluded from SLA computation unless both parties agree otherwise.

One suggested addition from my side: include an automatic model-fallback rule in the SLO addendum — if a region's rolling 30-minute snapshot p95 exceeds threshold and we detect it's due to sudden load (not provider outage), Redwood will automatically route to a lower-latency model variant for up to 60 minutes while we remediate. This reduces the chance of breach while keeping user experience acceptable. If fallback is used more than twice in a 30-day window, it will trigger a post-mortem and, if needed, crediting based on the original measurement.

I've linked the HubSpot deal in the related links so CS and legal can reference the pilot artifacts: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-123456

— Karthik

A few quick items from Brightline ops:
- We agree to the 30-day pilot (compute both baseline and tiered metrics in parallel).
- Please include at least two historical launch days in the backtest (we'll share timestamps).
- We want the canary to be limited to our US region only for the first month.
- Scheduling: Wed 12/3 10:00am PT works for a call; send an invite and the pilot timeline doc.

If all goes well we'll fold the tiered snapshotting language into the SLA addendum and finalize the deal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
